title: Westfield planning board kills $3 billion data center project
key_facts: Westfield's planning board voted unanimously on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 not to extend the special permit, due to expire at the end of October, for Servistar Realties' planned $3 billion hyperscale data centre on more than 150 acres, pursued in the city since 2019 (Boston.com).
The board granted the original permits in October 2021 and said the company had made little headway and had not shown good cause for an extension.
Chair William Carellas said the company never bought the property, which was central to his decision.

Paul Corey, who represented Servistar, blamed the lack of state tax incentives (Massachusetts codified sales tax breaks in 2024; Gov. Maura Healey paused applications this summer) and federal tariffs; the board was unmoved.
Members also cited procedural lapses: Servistar let its limited liability company status expire in late 2024 and never recorded its special permit at the Hampden County Registry of Deeds.

Servistar has 20 days to appeal; the decision effectively ends large-scale data-centre development in Westfield for now, as the City Council approved a one-year moratorium in July from which this project was exempt because it was already underway.
quote_evidence: A planned hyperscale data center in Westfield has been struck down after the city’s planning board voted Tuesday not to extend the developer’s special permit, which is set to expire at the end of October.
But the company never bought the property.
Servistar has 20 days to appeal the board’s decision under state law.
why_it_matters_hint: A $3 billion data centre plan died because the developer never bought the land or kept its paperwork in order, in a state where towns are slowing data-centre projects.
notes: Board vote was Tuesday 13 Oct 2026, three days before the window. The developer's principal did not respond to Boston.com.
